items.content: Three simulated crystal graph datasets were successfully generated: a large unlabeled pre-training set (5,000 samples), a fine-tuning set with scarce positive samples (2,000 samples, 5% positive ratio
items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode B (methodological and analytical validation of the simulated data framework), the report goes significantly beyond a baseline dataset description by performing a forensic audit of the 5,000/2,000/1,000 crystal graph splits—verifying exact positive counts (99 and 43), zero cross-split permutation duplicates, 28-element magnetic/ligand compositions, and generator artifacts such as asymmetric edges and chemically unrealistic stoichiometries. Crucially, after rigorously proving via 84 chi-square tests, univariate AUCs, and 5,000-sample cross-validation that the provided synthetic labels are statistically independent of graph structure, the agent constructs a controlled structure-defined positive control (100 fine-tuning positives at 5.4%, 50 hidden candidate positives at 5.6%, and systematic 10-to-100-shot budgets) on the same graphs. This thoroughly validates rich self-supervised representation learning from the 5,000 unlabeled graphs (+0.25 10-shot AUC gain and strong linear probes) and quantitative candidate discovery evaluation (14–18/50 hits@50, p = 0.001), raising critical physical and statistical insights beyond the baseline framework.

items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode B (architectural design and mechanistic analysis), the report faithfully implements all core components of the search engine in pure PyTorch: a three-layer gated CGCNN encoder with Gaussian RBF edge expansion, LayerNorm, and per-layer residual connections; a two-layer MLP decoder for self-supervised masked-node reconstruction (preventing trivial skip-connection copying); and a downstream classifier with global mean-max pooling and Dropout(0.3) regularization. Going beyond standard architectural descriptions, the report empirically validates the underlying mechanisms on a structural positive control via a 3- vs. 6-layer residual ablation confirming optimization collapse without skip connections, linear probes quantifying learned topological and chemical features over random initialization, and few-shot label-efficiency sweeps comparing frozen, fine-tuned, and from-scratch training. Minor omissions—such as lacking an explicit gating-off ablation and using only two seeds in the depth study alongside slight hyperparameter variations (Dropout 0.3 vs. 0.25)—keep the score from higher tiers, meriting a 68.

items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective), the agent uses a sound methodology and achieves pre-training convergence (on a 3.32 to 2.84 cross-entropy scale rather than the target figure's 0.10 to 0.00 loss), but fails to meet the criterion's downstream benchmarks on the provided labels. Fine-tuning validation balanced accuracy remains near chance (~50%) with severe overfitting (>40% gap), and candidate screening produces zero high-confidence predictions (p > 0.9) instead of the ~60% discovery rate, demonstrating positive discovery only on a self-constructed control task.
